an3.15:2.1: _Pacetana_, meaning “forethought”, often describes gods, kings, or sages; indeed seeral are named Pracetas. However, Sanskrit dictionaries also note the term _pracetṛ_ as “charioteer”. Both meanings apply here, as he is taking forethought in building a chariot.
an3.15:2.3: Kauṭilya says, “War at a pre-announced time and place is the most righteous” (Arthaśāstra 10.3.26). Military campaigns were timed with the seasons to procure advantages in relation to crops, weather, flooding, and so on (9.1.34–52).
an3.15:2.4: The scale of military preparations are charmingly minimal: the king personally attends to a pair of wheels. | Here, a _ratha_ is two-wheeled, hence “chariot” rather than “wagon”. See too Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa 12.2.2.2.
